text:
Not all low mood is depression. Demoralization describes a sense of being unable to cope with a stressful situation. Its hallmark is subjective incompetence: the person is willing to act but unsure how to move forward. Pleasure helps tell the two apart. In demoralization, the capacity for pleasure is usually still present. In a depressive episode, it usually fades. Poor concentration, low energy and poor sleep are usually absent in demoralization but may be present in depression. The two can occur separately or together, so the distinction is a prompt to look closer, never a reason to overlook depression. Demoralization is classified in ICD-11 but not in DSM-5-TR.

Where the evidence stops:
• This is a short commentary by one author, not a systematic review, and many of the studies it draws on involved people with medical illnesses such as cancer, Parkinson disease or inflammatory bowel disease.

Key source: de Figueiredo, J. M. (2026). The demoralization construct in clinical practice and research. The Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, 87(2). https://doi.org/10.4088/JCP.26com16383
